VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package. VHA Physician Total Rewards. This Full Time (40 hours) position is located at the John D. Dingell VA Medical Center in Detroit, Michigan. Join a team of Pathologist providers, some full time VA, others part-time with the affiliate Wayne State University School of Medicine.

The extent of duties performed by the staff pathologist in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine at the Detroit VA Healthcare system is the dependent on the individual's documented training, certification and credentialing.

The potential breadth of duties is described below: Surgical pathology: Derive diagnoses from gross and microscopic examination of tissues and other materials submitted by biopsy or surgical procedures. This includes interpretation of tissues submitted intraoperatively for frozen section diagnosis.

Advanced subspecialty training in surgical pathology may provide additional expertise. Hematopathology: Provide expert hematologic diagnostic interpretations of blood, bone marrow, lymph node and fluid preparations. Provide interpretations of serum and urine electrophoreses.

Dermatopathology: Provide expert diagnostic interpretation of inflammatory, melanocytic and non-melanocytic lesions in skin biopsies and excisions. Genitourinary pathology: Provide expert diagnostic interpretation of diseases involving the urinary and reproductive organs.

Gastrointestinal pathology: Provide expert diagnostic interpretation of diseases involving the oral-esophageal, stomach, upper and lower intestinal tract as well as liver and pancreas. Clinical Pathology: Understand organization and principles of clinical laboratory testing.

Provide consultation regarding chemistry analytic, hematologic, microbiologic, molecular diagnostic and blood bank issues. Advanced subspecialty training in clinical pathology may provide additional expertise. Examples listed below. Transfusion medicine: Provide expert consultation and guidance regarding blood product transfusion issues.

Molecular diagnostics: Provide expert consultation and guidance regarding molecular genetic testing and interpretations. Autopsy pathology: Derive cause of death and identify diseased tissues by post-mortem necropsy and tissue examination. This function includes supervision of dieners and resident pathologists.

Cytopathology: Derive diagnoses from microscopic examination of cellular material from gynecologic and non-gynecologic sources prepared for cytologic examination. This includes assessment of specimen adequacy and examination of prepared cell-block material. Duties may also include performance of fine-needle aspiration of palpable nodules.

Administrative: Participate in laboratory oversight to the extent assigned and serve on institutional level committees and workgroups. Quality: Meet defined service and institutional level quality performance measures. Participate in or initiate laboratory or institutional quality improvement and management programs.

Educational: Provide teaching, supervision and guidance of technologists, technicians fellows and pathology residents in the aspects of the clinical duties described above. Participate in interdisciplinary educational conferences involving clinical pathologic correlation.

Research: Support VHA research mission through participation in collaborative or self-initiated research projects. Education Debt Reduction Program (Student Loan Repayment): Learn more. EDRP Authorized: Former EDRP participants ineligible to apply for incentive. Contact at VISN10HRCCOE@va.gov, the EDRP Coordinator for questions/assistance.

Pay: Competitive salary, annual performance bonus, regular salary increases Paid Time Off: 50-55 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year and possible 5 day paid absence for CME) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory CME: Possible $1,000 per year reimbursement (must be full-time with board certification) Malpractice: Free liability protection with tail coverage provided Contract: No Physician Employment Contract and no significant restriction on moonlighting Work Schedule: Monday thru Friday 8:00 am to 4:30 pm
To qualify for this position, you must meet the basic requirements as well as any additional requirements (if applicable) listed in the job announcement. Applicants pending the completion of training or license requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Currently employed physician(s) in VA who met the requirements for appointment under the previous qualification standard at the time of their initial appointment are deemed to have met the basic requirements of the occupation.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

The degree must have been obtained from one of the schools approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs for the year in which the course of study was completed. Current, full and unrestricted license to practice medicine or surgery in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Approved residencies are: (1) Those approved by the accrediting bodies for graduate medical education, the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA), in the list published for the year the residency, or fellowship if applicable, was completed; OR (2) One year of post medical school training (internship, first year of residency, or transitional year residency) approved by ACGME or AOA followed by two years of post-training independent practice (performing under a full and unrestricted license) in the United States; OR (3) Non-US residency training programs followed by a minimum of three years of verified independent practice in the United States (performing under a full and unrestricted license) performing duties related to the position they are applying for (United States fellowships would be creditable towards this requirement), which the local Medical Staff Executive Committee deems to have provided the applicant with appropriate professional training and believes has exposed the Physician to an appropriate range of patient care experiences.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

In rare and unusual circumstances, the Facility Director can submit a memo to the VISN Director through the VISN Chief Medical Officer, who may approve requests for reasonable exceptions to the residency training requirement for Physicians whose composite record of experience, accomplishments, performance, and qualifications warrant such action.

Proficiency in spoken and written English. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/.

Physical Requirements: Heavy lifting and carrying (45+ lbs.); As needed - Straight pulling, pulling handover hand, pushing and reaching above shoulders, walking, standing, crawling, kneeling, repeated bending, climbing using both legs and arms; use of fingers and both hands required; ability for rapid mental and muscular coordination simultaneously; near vision correctable at 13'-16" to Jaeger 1 to 4; far vision correctable in one eye to 20/20 and to 20/40 in the other; depth perception; ability to distinguish basic colors; hearing (aid permitted); working closely with others; working alone; protracted or irregular hours of work.

Job Summary Each year, MedSchoolCoach supports more than a thousand pre-medical and medical students as they pursue successful careers in medicine. As physicians who have personally navigated the medical school and residency application process, we provide expert guidance grounded in firsthand experience.

We are seeking highly accomplished physicians to serve as Master Physician Advisors . This role is designed for physicians with extensive admissions expertise, significant mentoring experience, and a passion for helping future physicians succeed.

Master Advisors serve as trusted experts, providing strategic, high-level advising to applicants throughout every stage of the medical school and residency application process.

This opportunity is ideal for retired physicians or physicians who have transitioned away from full-time clinical practice and are interested in dedicating 20+ hours per week to mentoring the next generation of physicians. Responsibilities Serve as a senior advisor to pre-medical students applying to medical school.

Advise medical students applying to residency through the ERAS and NRMP Match process (when applicable). Conduct comprehensive one-on-one advising sessions focused on application strategy, competitiveness, career planning, and professional development.

Provide expert guidance on school selection, application timelines, interview preparation, and admissions strategy. Collaborate with writing advisors to develop and refine personal statements, secondary essays, activities descriptions, and residency application materials. Conduct high-level mock interviews and deliver detailed, actionable feedback.

Share firsthand admissions committee and residency selection committee insights to help students better understand evaluation criteria and strengthen their candidacy. Participate in webinars, educational content creation, blogs, workshops, and other thought leadership initiatives.

Serve as a subject matter expert and ambassador for MedSchoolCoach 's advising program. Required Qualifications MD degree from an accredited U.S. medical school. Successful completion of an accredited U.S. residency training program. Significant experience serving on a medical school admissions committee and/or residency selection committee.

Minimum of two years of advising, mentoring, teaching, admissions, or residency selection experience. Deep understanding of the AMCAS application process. Strong knowledge of the ERAS application and NRMP Match processes. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.

Demonstrated ability to mentor, coach, and inspire students from diverse backgrounds. Highly available to students (20+ hours per week). Comfortable using Microsoft Word, Zoom, Google Meet, Gmail, and other communication platforms. Preferred Qualifications Experience in academic medicine, medical education, or faculty leadership.

Experience interviewing and selecting medical school or residency applicants. Previous experience advising students through successful medical school admissions and/or residency matching. Retired physicians and physicians practicing part-time are strongly encouraged to apply.

About MedSchoolCoach MedSchoolCoach is a rapidly growing EdTech company dedicated to helping future physicians achieve their goals through expert advising, tutoring, software, and educational resources.

Founded and led by physicians, MedSchoolCoach has become one of the largest organizations in the medical education space, reaching nearly half of all prospective medical students each year through one or more of our products and services.

Working at MedSchoolCoach We are a distributed team of physicians, educators, advisors, tutors, and entrepreneurs who share a passion for improving healthcare through education. We value collaboration, initiative, integrity, and a genuine commitment to student success.

Our team enjoys the flexibility of remote work while making a meaningful impact on the next generation of physicians. We strive to create an environment where every team member can contribute their expertise, continue growing professionally, and maintain a healthy work-life balance.

I think this version creates a much clearer distinction between your standard Physician Advisor role and the Master level. It positions these physicians as true experts whose value comes not only from being physicians, but from their admissions committee experience, residency selection expertise, and strategic advising capabilities.

It should also make sourcing easier because candidates can immediately recognize that this is a more prestigious, senior opportunity. Originally posted on Himalayas

Are you ready to help reinvent primary care with a focus on lifestyle medicine and longevity? As Amenities Health ’s Concierge Longevity Physician, you’ll not only deliver comprehensive primary care, but also actively shape the evolution of our premium concierge practice from day one.

The focus of this clinical role is on a Concierge Longevity Program which includes elements of traditional primary care, time to build relationships with your patients, and time to focus on the latest in longevity assessments and treatments. What you’ll do:
Deliver longitudinal, relationship-based care to a curated virtual panel (~1,000 members) — from preventive health and chronic conditions to complex care coordination, lifestyle medicine, root cause diagnosis, and advanced wellness.
Focus on modern longevity approaches based in lifestyle medicine with bandwidth to contemplate and advise patients on emerging pharmacological (e.g., GLP-1s, Category 1 Peptides) and non-pharmacological (e.g., red-light therapy, hot/cold plunges, hyperbaric) therapies.
Lead and contribute to the continued development of digital workflows, messaging norms, scheduling design, white-glove service protocols, and advanced clinical offerings.
Serve as a clinical voice in shaping practice culture, communication standards, and patient engagement—in a nimble, highly-motivated startup where your ideas directly impact care delivery.
Enjoy protected time for same-day urgent care, in-depth consults (50-min new appointments, 25-min follow-ups), and flexible administrative blocks—with zero legacy headaches or RVU churn.
What Makes This Role Different
Your panel, your pace: focus on quality of relationships, not volume of visits.
You’ll help build; not just participate. From EMR customizations to new service lines and wellness offerings, your clinical feedback directly drives our growth.
Join a company at the intersection of primary care, concierge medicine, longevity, AI-supported virtual care, and premium member services.
No maneuvering long clinic hallways, no “surprise” overbooks—just fully remote, modern, and optimized care that acknowledges that the best patient loyalty comes from physician loyalty.
As a direct (cash-pay) model, insurance billing workflows will not be a part of the physician’s role, giving you more time to focus on excellent patient care

100% remote, flexibly scheduled position (standard hours at launch, with future options to customize your week)
Panel capped at 1,000 for deep relationships—with full team support, modern EMR, and administrative help
The resources of major partner institutions (i.e., a robust referral network to supplement your care leadership)
100% company-paid health insurance for you and/or family
A 401K program
PTO package, monthly wellness days, and annual off-sites
A mix of base annual salary and performance bonus for total cash compensation
Generous stock options: true ownership in our collective future

US board-certified MD/DO in Internal Medicine or Family Medicine
3+ years in outpatient practice experience
Active medical license (or eligibility)
A service-oriented approach to patient care (i.e., a willingness, patience and joy in engaging patients, at their level, on their questions and interests)
A willingness to engage and stay up-to-date on topics like longevity, advanced testing, wearable data and monitoring, mental health, women's/men's health, and more

A social media presence, including LinkedIn, X, Instagram, etc.
Medical license in current and expansion states (NC, TX, CA, IN) or multi-state licensure
Experience in virtual care and/or concierge, DPC, or membership-based models
Strong track record of delivering outstanding patient experience and clinical excellence
An openness to new care frameworks and innovations and a commitment to comprehensive service to the patient
Comfort and curiosity with the latest in health tech: AI documentation, wearables, advanced diagnostics, lifestyle medicine, longevity, root-cause approaches
Commitment to collaborating, iterating, and building a better model—not just working in the old one
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Amenities Health is on a mission to build lasting loyalty in healthcare through our white-labeled concierge membership services for leading health systems.

We believe that physicians sit at the center of that experience, and our model is designed to give them the time, tools, and operational support they need to deliver exceptional, relationship-driven care.

Founded by a physician executive with deep experience in major health systems and consumer-facing healthcare innovation, Amenities Health blends technology, care services, and clinical operations to create a best-in-class, scalable concierge care experience.

Our virtual-first, membership-based model pairs market-leading digital infrastructure with a high-touch service approach, enabling physicians to build trusted, long-term relationships with a thoughtfully capped panel of patients.

As we scale with some of the country’s top healthcare brands, we’re setting a new standard for what modern longevity care can feel like - for patients, for physicians, and for the systems that support them. We invite clinicians who value time, connection, and care excellence to help us shape the future of concierge care.

Unlike most technology companies who are trying to increase panel sizes, we’re capping them at 1,000. We believe that, with enough time, physicians can and should develop loyal, trusted relationships with their patients… which is an excellent business strategy. Originally posted on Himalayas

To qualify for this position, your resume must state sufficient experience and/or education, to perform the duties of the specific position for which you are applying.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer and part time experience.

You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. BASIC REQUIREMENT(S): Degree: Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine or equivalent from a school in the United States or Canada.

This degree must have been accredited by the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association; Association of American Medical Colleges; Liaison Committee on Medical Education; Commission on Osteopathic College Accreditation of the American Osteopathic Association, or an accrediting body recognized by the U.S.

Department of Education at the time the degree was obtained. Degree from Foreign Medical School: A Doctor of Medicine or equivalent degree from a foreign medical school must provide education and medical knowledge equivalent to accredited schools in the United States.

Evidence of equivalency to accredited schools in the United States is demonstrated by permanent certification by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates, a fifth pathway certificate for Americans who completed premedical education in the United States and graduate education in a foreign country, or successful completion of the U.S.

Medical Licensing Examination. Licensure: For all grade levels and positions, applicants must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration as a Physician from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States.

Graduate Training: Subsequent to obtaining a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree, a candidate must have had at least 1 year of supervised experience providing direct service in a clinical setting, i.e., a 1-year internship or the first year of a residency program in a hospital or an institution accredited for such training.

For purposes of this standard, graduate training programs include only those internship, residency, and fellowship programs that are approved by accrediting bodies recognized within the United States or Canada. Descriptions of such programs are described below.

An internship program involves broadly based clinical practice in which physicians acquire experience in treating a variety of medical problems under supervision (e.g., internal medicine, surgery, general practice, obstetrics-gynecology, and pediatrics).

Such programs are in hospitals or other institutions accredited for internship training by a recognized body of the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA).

A residency program involves training in a specialized field of medicine in a hospital or an institution accredited for training in the specialty by a recognized body of the American Medical Association (AMA), American Osteopathic Association (AOA) or Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME).

A fellowship program involves advanced training (beyond residency training) in a given medical specialty in either a clinical or research setting in a hospital or an institution accredited in the United States for such training.

In addition, to the Basic Requirements, you must also meet the Minimum Qualifications stated below- For GS-15 - 5 years of graduate training in the specialty of the position to be filled or equivalent experience and training.

Substitution of Experience for Residency Training: Experience may not be substituted for residency training that is essential for the performance of specialized duties. For example, specialists such as psychiatrists and surgeons must complete the number of years of accredited residency training required in their respective specialties.

An exception may be made when a peer panel of physicians (subject-matter experts) determines and documents that the knowledge, skills, and abilities acquired in professional medical practice are equivalent to those acquired during the same period of time in a graduate training program.

The Neurologist will provide virtual consultations, analyze medical history, symptoms and findings of patients' health condidtion, treatments, medication and patient education via Tele-Health remotely.

Administrative Duties include but are not limited to: Responds to and conducts assigned administrative duties to facilitate the performance of Neurology services including: Writes Medical Orders and prescriptions for non-controlled substances, as necessary, for the care of the patient in accordance with Federal and State law and approval of the supervising Physician.

Documents care provided in the Computerized Patient Record System (CPRS) in accordance with Valley Coastal Bend Health Care System requirements. Documents the detailed, targeted, initial history and physical examination required for evaluation in the electronic tool(s) required by VA.

Obtains consent and documents procedures performed for which the physician is responsible. Provides education and counseling of patients and families in preventive care, medical conditions, and the use of prescribed treatments and drugs.

Clinical Duties include but are not limited to: Responds to and completes consults received for the evaluation of Neurology including: Performs a comprehensive, detailed, targeted, initial history and physical examination in compliance with national guidelines.

Consults other disciplines, as necessary, to complete the patient evaluation. Carries out health promotion and disease prevention activities including education and shared decision-making.

Competence in neurological procedures is desirable and documentation of procedures within the past 12 months will be requested reflective of the scope of privileges requested. Participates in all VISN and national level efforts in neurological programs.

## Allgemeinarzt/-ärztin 80-100% in Schiers gesucht – Ihre Expertise für eine ganzheitliche Patientenversorgung
Einsatzort: Schiers und UmgebungEinsatzbeginn: Ab sofort oder nach Vereinbarung
Allgemeinarzt Schiers gesucht.
Schiers liegt malerisch im Prättigau in Graubünden und besticht durch seine idyllische Lage inmitten einer reizvollen Berglandschaft. Die Gemeinde ist durch die Rhätische Bahn sowie mehrere Buslinien gut mit den umliegenden Regionen verbunden und ermöglicht so eine komfortable Mobilität. Als Arbeitsort bietet Schiers Ihnen eine ausgezeichnete Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Natur mit hoher Lebensqualität sowie guten Bedingungen für kleine und mittlere Unternehmen.
Als Allgemeinarzt Schiers übernehmen Sie eine wichtige Rolle in der Betreuung von Patienten, und gleichzeitig begleiten Sie Menschen über längere Zeit, sodass eine vertrauensvolle Beziehung entsteht. Dabei arbeiten Sie nicht nur im direkten Kontakt mit Patienten, sondern auch im Team, damit Diagnosen klar sind und Behandlungen gut geplant werden können. So entsteht eine Betreuung, die sowohl sicher als auch verständlich ist.
Im Alltag erleben Sie viele verschiedene Situationen, und dadurch bleibt Ihre Arbeit abwechslungsreich, während Sie gleichzeitig Verantwortung übernehmen. Ihr Wissen hilft Ihnen, sodass Sie schnell reagieren können, und gleichzeitig sorgt Ihre ruhige Art dafür, dass Patienten sich gut aufgehoben fühlen.
Unser Temporärbüro Pflege Schiers unterstützt Sie dabei, eine Stelle zu finden, die zu Ihnen passt, sodass Sie flexibel arbeiten können und gleichzeitig eine stabile Perspektive haben.
iPersonal AG ist ein Temporärbüro, das sich auf die Vermittlung von hochqualifizierten Fachkräften spezialisiert hat und Unternehmen dabei unterstützt, ihre Personalbedürfnisse zu decken.
Mehr Informationen finden Sie hier:[https://www.med-ipersonal.ch](https://www.med-ipersonal.ch)
### Ihre Aufgaben im Praxisalltag
Im täglichen Einsatz arbeiten Sie direkt mit Patienten, und gleichzeitig sorgen Sie dafür, dass alle Abläufe klar bleiben, sodass eine sichere Betreuung möglich ist.
Zu Beginn führen Sie Gespräche, damit Beschwerden genau erfasst werden und ein klares Bild entsteht. Danach treffen Sie Entscheidungen, sodass Patienten gezielt behandelt werden können und schnell Hilfe erhalten.
Während der weiteren Betreuung begleiten Sie Patienten über längere Zeit, sodass Entwicklungen erkannt werden und Fortschritte sichtbar sind. Gleichzeitig stimmen Sie sich mit anderen Fachpersonen ab, damit alle Schritte gut zusammenpassen und keine Lücken entstehen.
Auch die Beratung gehört zu Ihrem Alltag, und dabei erklären Sie Zusammenhänge so, dass Patienten ihre Situation verstehen und aktiv mitarbeiten können. Gleichzeitig achten Sie darauf, dass Abläufe klar bleiben, sodass der Alltag ruhig und gut organisiert ist.
### Das bringen Sie mit
Für diese Position bringen Sie nicht nur Fachwissen mit, sondern auch die Fähigkeit, ruhig zu arbeiten, sodass Sie auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen sicher handeln können.
Sie haben ein abgeschlossenes Medizinstudium, und gleichzeitig kennen Sie den Alltag aus Praxis oder Spital, sodass Sie schnell Entscheidungen treffen können. Ihre Erfahrung hilft Ihnen, Probleme früh zu erkennen, und gleichzeitig bleiben Sie strukturiert, damit alles gut läuft.
Neben der fachlichen Seite ist auch Ihre Persönlichkeit wichtig, und deshalb arbeiten Sie selbstständig, während Sie gleichzeitig im Team eingebunden sind. So entsteht eine gute Zusammenarbeit, die den Alltag erleichtert.
Klare Kommunikation ist ebenfalls entscheidend, damit Patienten sich verstanden fühlen und Vertrauen aufbauen können. Gute Deutschkenntnisse helfen Ihnen dabei, sodass alle Informationen klar vermittelt werden.
### Das erwartet Sie
Hier erwartet Sie eine Stelle, die Ihnen Sicherheit bietet, und gleichzeitig haben Sie die Möglichkeit, sich weiterzuentwickeln, sodass Sie langfristig zufrieden sind.

### **Ihr Wirkungsfeld** ###
* Gesamtverantwortung für die standortübergreifende HNO-Klinik der LUKS Gruppe (medizinisch, organisatorisch und wirtschaftlich) sowie Führung der ärztlichen, logopädischen, audiologischen, neurootologischen, MPA- und administrativen Teams unter Einbezug der leitenden Mitarbeitenden
* Strategische und konzeptionelle Weiterentwicklung der HNO-Klinik mit Fokus auf Roboter-Chirurgie, endoskopische Ohr-, NNH- und Schädelbasischirurgie, Cochlea- und Mittelohr-Implantat-Chirurgie sowie standortübergreifende Strategien für bestehende und zukünftige Standorte
* Sicherstellung höchster Qualitätsstandards in Diagnostik und Therapie, Förderung von Innovationen, neuen Technologien, klinischer Forschung, universitärer Lehre sowie der Weiter- und Fortbildung im Rahmen der anerkannten Weiterbildungsstätte Kategorie A
* Verantwortung für Budget, Ressourcen und die wirtschaftliche Entwicklung der Klinik, Pflege und Ausbau des Zuweisernetzwerks, Förderung der interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit sowie Repräsentation der Klinik und Stärkung regionaler, nationaler und internationaler Netzwerke
### **Ihre Erfahrung** ###
* Facharzttitel (FMH oder äquivalent) für Otorhinolaryngologie mit Schwerpunkttitel Hals- und Gesichtschirurgie sowie breiter, ausgewiesener Expertise im gesamten HNO-Spektrum und eigenem Schwerpunkt in mindestens einer Subspezialität
* Hohe operative Kompetenz in mindestens einer HNO-Subspezialität sowie Führungserfahrung an einem Zentrumsspital oder in einem universitären Umfeld mit wissenschaftlichem Profil
* Nachgewiesene Fähigkeit zur Umsetzung eigener Forschungsideen, insbesondere in der klinischen und universitären Forschung, verbunden mit ausgeprägten Führungs-, Sozial- und Kommunikationskompetenzen sowie Freude an interdisziplinärer Zusammenarbeit
* Fundierte Kenntnisse des schweizerischen Gesundheits- und Versicherungswesens, betriebswirtschaftliches Verständnis (idealerweise mit Führungs- oder Managementausbildung) sowie Offenheit gegenüber Digitalisierung
### **Ihre Perspektiven** ###
\- Leitung und Weiterentwicklung der HNO- und Kopf-Halschirurgie inklusive Phoniatrie, Neuro-Otologie und Päd-Audiologie mit einem exzellenten Team und modernster Infrastruktur (Robotik, mikroskopische und endoskopische Chirurgie)
\- Grosser Gestaltungsspielraum zur Weiterentwicklung der HNO-Klinik und ihrer Subdisziplinen über die verschiedenen Standorte der LUKS-Gruppe sowie das Kinderspital LUKS hinweg
\- Spannende Führungsfunktion innerhalb einer dynamischen universitären Spitalgruppe mit klarer Zukunftsstrategie
\- Es werden nur Direktbewerbungen bis zum 31. Oktober 2026 berücksichtigt. Bewerbungen via Personalvermittler können nicht berücksichtigt werden

Die Universitätsklinik für Neurologie ist die grösste neurologische Klinik der Schweiz und bietet eine qualitativ hochstehende Behandlung sowohl in der neurologischen Grundversorgung als auch in der hochspezialisierten Medizin. Ambulant werden jährlich über 30'000 Patient:innen und stationär ca. 2'000 Patient:innen behandelt.

Der Kompetenzbereich für neuromuskuläre Erkrankungen am Inselspital ist eine der grössten universitätsklinischen Abteilungen in der Schweiz und widmet sich der Abklärung und Behandlung von Patient:innen mit einem breiten neuromuskulären Krankheitsspektrum.
Als kosek-anerkanntes Referenzzentrum koordinieren wir zusammen mit anderen Fachstellen und Patientenorganisationen die Versorgung bei seltenen neuromuskulären Krankheiten.
Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir eine Fachärztin:arzt Neurologie mit besonderem Interesse und fundiertem Wissen sowohl in der neuromuskulären (inkl. elektrophysiologischer) Diagnostik als auch der Behandlung neuromuskulärer Patienten.
**Das erwartet Sie**
* Vielseitiges Patient:innenspektrum im Kompetenzzentrum für neuromuskuläre Erkrankungen
* Attraktive Möglichkeiten zur fachlichen Weiterentwicklung im Bereich der ambulanten neuromuskulären Patient:innenversorgung.
* Anteilige Tätigkeit in einem anderen Bereich der Klinik für Neurologie nach Absprache möglich
* Möglichkeit der Mitarbeit im Bereich Lehre und Forschung falls gewünscht
* Übernahme von Leitungsfunktionen im Verlauf
* Ein motiviertes interdisziplinäres und interprofessionelles Team von Care Manager:innen und Physiotherapeut:innen unterstützt Sie in Ihrer Tätigkeit
**Das bringen Sie mit**
* Facharzttitel FMH Neurologie oder äquivalent
* Abgeschlossene elektrophysiologische ENMG-Ausbildung (Zertifikat SGKN ENMG) mit vertiefter Kenntnis und Interesse an neuromuskulären Erkrankungen mit idealerweise längerer Expertise in diesem Bereich
* Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift, idealerweise auch gute mündliche Französischkenntnisse. Weitere Fremdsprachenkenntnisse sind von Vorteil
* Selbstständigkeit und Teamfähigkeit
* Interesse und Fertigkeiten auch eigene Sprechstundenbereiche zu managen und klinisch sowie planerisch zu gestallten
* Freude an der Supervision, Weiterbildung und Förderung von Assistenzärzt:innen
* Hohe Sozialkompetenz, patient:innenorientierte Arbeitsweise sowie sehr gute kommunikative Fähigkeiten
* Selbstständige, strukturierte und verantwortungsbewusste Arbeitsweise bei gleichzeitig ausgeprägter Teamfähigkeit
**Unser Angebot**
* Teilnahme an interdisziplinären Fallkonferenzen und Expertenboards
* Möglichkeit zur jederzeitigen Supervision durch die Leiter der jeweiligen Schwerpunkte
* Enge Zusammenarbeit mit zuweisenden Ärzt, Hausärzt, interprofessionellen Behandlungsteams sowie weiteren Fachdisziplinen des Inselspitals
* Teilnahme am allgemeinen neurologischen Notfall- und Bereitschaftsdienst
* Mitarbeit in einem engagierten und kollegialen Team mit hoher fachlicher Expertise sowie strukturierter Einarbeitung in die ambulanten Abläufe
* Arbeiten in einer modernen baulichen und digitalen Infrastruktur

réso.ne est le nouveau réseau de santé ambulatoire de référence du canton de Neuchâtel.
Né de la volonté du Réseau hospitalier neuchâtelois (RHNe) de renforcer durablement l'offre de soins de proximité, réso.ne s'inscrit au cœur de la politique sanitaire cantonale 2025-2030. Sa mission est de garantir à la population un accès coordonné, performant et pérenne aux soins ambulatoires, en complémentarité étroite avec la médecine de ville et l'ensemble des acteurs du système de santé.
réso.ne développe un réseau intégré de centres médicaux répartis sur le territoire cantonal, notamment à Neuchâtel, La Chaux-de-Fonds, Fleurier et Geneveys-sur-Coffrane. Cette organisation favorise la continuité des soins, la coordination entre les professionnels et une prise en charge fluide des patients, qu'il s'agisse de consultations programmées, de suivi longitudinal ou de situations urgentes non vitales.
Grâce à un partenariat fort avec le RHNe, réso.ne bénéficie d'un accès privilégié aux expertises hospitalières, aux projets médicaux innovants, à des outils de coordination modernes et l-accès facilité à la formation continue et à la documentation. Cette collaboration permet de renforcer les liens entre les acteurs, et à améliorer le parcours de soins des patients.
Au-delà de sa mission clinique, réso.ne place la formation et la transmission des savoirs au cœur de son développement. Description de l'entreprise La Clinique de Genolier fait partie de Médecin assistant ou chef de clinique adjoint en médecine nucléaire 80\\-100% (ISFM\\-B) Description de l'entreprise La Clinique de Genolier fait partie de Swiss Medical Network, un réseau comprenant près de 25 hôpitaux et plus de 70 centres de santé en Suisse.

Le Service de médecine nucléaire de la Clinique de Genolier est reconnu comme centre de formation postgraduée ISFM de catégorie B, pour une durée maximale de deux ans. Il propose un poste de médecin assistant ou de chef de clinique adjoint.

Le centre est installé dans le bâtiment du Genolier Innovation Hub, au cœur du campus de Genolier, à proximité immédiate des services de radio\\-oncologie et de radiologie.

Il est l'un des deux centres européens d'excellence de GE HealthCare en imagerie moléculaire et en théranostique, ainsi que l'un des membres fondateurs du réseau international de centres d'innovation de GE HealthCare.

Le centre collabore activement avec plusieurs institutions hospitalières suisses et régionales, notamment les Hôpitaux universitaires de Genève, l'Hôpital cantonal de Lucerne, les hôpitaux de Nyon et de Morges, le Centre hospitalier Alpes Léman et le Centre Léon Bérard à Lyon.

Il développe un programme de recherche actif dans les domaines de l'imagerie avancée, de l'intelligence artificielle et des essais cliniques. Il accueille également des étudiants issus des écoles polytechniques ainsi que des chercheurs expérimentés.

Le premier exemplaire commercial du PET total\\-body OMNI 128 cm, la première mise à niveau commerciale au monde du StarGuide vers la configuration GX Dual\\-Sided, ainsi qu'une unité de théranostique avec chambres de radioprotection seront opérationnels au cours des prochains mois.

Le centre propose une gamme complète d'examens diagnostiques destinés aux patients adultes, notamment en oncologie, en cardiologie par PET et en neurologie. Il réalise également l'ensemble des examens conventionnels de médecine nucléaire, ainsi que des protocoles complets d'imagerie multimodale incluant le CT diagnostique.

Vous intégrerez une équipe composée de cinq médecins cadres, dont deux bénéficient d'une affiliation universitaire : l'un auprès des Hôpitaux universitaires de Genève et l'autre en qualité de responsable de l'unité de théranostique du Centre Léon Bérard à Lyon.

Vous serez également encadré par des spécialistes titulaires d'un double titre FMH, notamment en médecine nucléaire et radiologie ou en médecine nucléaire et cardiologie. Description du poste Le centre recherche un médecin souhaitant obtenir, à terme, le titre postgrade fédéral de spécialiste en médecine nucléaire.

Le poste est ouvert aux candidats avec ou sans expérience préalable dans la discipline. La supervision est assurée par les médecins cadres expérimentés du service.

Le poste garantit : un accès direct et progressif à l'ensemble des examens diagnostiques ; une participation active au programme de thérapie et de théranostique ; la participation aux colloques multidisciplinaires internes et externes à la Clinique ; l'intégration dans les réseaux de formation postgraduée ; un encadrement structuré conforme aux exigences du programme ISFM.

La définition et la réalisation d'un projet de recherche sont également encouragées, notamment afin de répondre aux exigences de la formation postgraduée ISFM.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

Current, full and unrestricted license to practice medicine or surgery in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

Unsere Patient\*innen brauchen Sie auch ausserhalb regulärer Bürozeiten? Dann haben Sie ein Anrecht auf eine faire Entschädigung. Für eine Nachtschicht erhalten Sie beispielsweise eine Zulage von mindestens 10 Franken pro Stunde, an Wochenenden und Feiertagen sogar bis zu 16.50 Franken.

So banal es klingt: Berufskleidung ist keine Freizeitkleidung. Nur fair also, wenn dies auch im Berufsalltag anerkannt wird. Bei uns gilt: Umkleidezeit ist Arbeitszeit. Pro Dienst stehen Ihnen 10 Minuten fürs Umkleiden zu.

Das UKBB ist familienfreundlich. Neben den gesetzlichen Familienzulagen zahlen wir zusätzliche Unterhaltszulagen für Kinder- und Jugendliche aus. Zum Beispiel stehen Ihnen auf ein 100%-Pensum gerechnet 400 Franken pro Monat für Ihr erstes Kind zu, für zwei Kinder insgesamt 500 Franken.

Während Ihrer Anstellung erhalten Sie stets den vollen Lohn, auch wenn Sie ausfallen. Darüber hinaus garantieren wir Ihnen bei Krankheit eine Lohnfortzahlung von 730 Tagen. Sollten Sie je eine stationäre Behandlung infolge Unfall benötigen, sind Sie erst noch Halbprivat versichert.

In den Restaurants am UKBB und Universitätsspital Basel kommen Sie in den Genuss eines Personalrabatts. Ein klassisches Mittagsmenü erhalten Mitarbeitende für CHF 9.70.

Duties for the Physician include, but are not limited to, the following: Reviewing individual results and rendering qualification determinations (e.g. fitness for duty as a compliance officer).

Applying epidemiologic principles, clinical and toxicologic information, and information and data management expertise to questions affecting worker safety and health. Providing assistance in the development, review and analysis of policies, guidelines, compliance procedures, and other documents requiring medical expertise.

Representing the agency at hearings and other legal proceedings that may require medical expertise concerning occupationally related illnesses and injuries. Developing informal or formal written responses to field consult requests for support, and documenting opinions using medical and scientific knowledge.

Preparing and delivering testimony in support of OSHA enforcement actions before Administrative Law Judges of the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Review Commission as needed.
This position has an Individual Occupational Requirement.

You must meet both the Basic Requirements and the Specialized Experience to qualify for the Physician (Medical Officer) as described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Medical Officer Series, 0602, Physician.https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0600/medical-officer-series-0602/ *Transcripts are required Degree: Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine or equivalent from a school in the United States or Canada.

This degree must have been accredited by the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association(external link); Association of American Medical Colleges(external link); Liaison Committee on Medical Education(external link); Commission on Osteopathic College Accreditation of the American Osteopathic Association(external link), or an accrediting body recognized by the U.S.

Department of Education(external link) at the time the degree was obtained. Degree from Foreign Medical School: A Doctor of Medicine or equivalent degree from a foreign medical school must provide education and medical knowledge equivalent to accredited schools in the United States.

Evidence of equivalency to accredited schools in the United States is demonstrated by permanent certification by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates(external link), a fifth pathway certificate for Americans who completed premedical education in the United States and graduate education in a foreign country, or successful completion of the U.S.

Medical Licensing Examination. Licensure: For all grade levels and positions, applicants must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration as a Physician from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States.

Graduate Training: Subsequent to obtaining a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree, a candidate must have had at least 1 year of supervised experience providing direct service in a clinical setting, i.e., a 1-year internship or the first year of a residency program in a hospital or an institution accredited for such training.

For purposes of this standard, graduate training programs include only those internship, residency, and fellowship programs that are approved by accrediting bodies recognized within the United States or Canada. Descriptions of such programs are described below.

An internship program involves broadly based clinical practice in which physicians acquire experience in treating a variety of medical problems under supervision (e.g., internal medicine, surgery, general practice, obstetrics-gynecology, and pediatrics).

Such programs are in hospitals or other institutions accredited for internship training by a recognized body of the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME)(external link).A residency program involves training in a specialized field of medicine in a hospital or an institution accredited for training in the specialty by a recognized body of the American Medical Association(external link), (AMA) or Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME)(external link).A fellowship program involves advanced training (beyond residency training) in a given medical specialty in either a clinical or research setting in a hospital or an institution accredited in the United States for such training.

AND Specialized Experience: Specialized Experience, is experience that has equipped the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled.

At the GS-14: Applicants must have at least 1 year of Specialized Experience equivalent to the GS-13 or higher, to qualify for this position.

For this position, examples of qualifying experience include: Participating in a residency program either in occupational medicine, general preventive medicine or aerospace medicine Conducting medical investigations and/or support activities with some supervision Participating in workgroups and/or seminars that relate to occupational medicine NOTE: IN DESCRIBING YOUR EXPERIENCE, PLEASE BE CLEAR AND SPECIFIC.

Currently employed physician(s) in VA who met the requirements for appointment under the previous qualification standard at the time of their initial appointment are deemed to have met the basic requirements of the occupation.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

The degree must have been obtained from one of the schools approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs for the year in which the course of study was completed. Current, full and unrestricted license to practice medicine or surgery in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Approved residencies are: (1) Those approved by the accrediting bodies for graduate medical education, the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA), in the list published for the year the residency, or fellowship if applicable, was completed; OR (2) One year of post medical school training (internship, first year of residency, or transitional year residency) approved by ACGME or AOA followed by two years of post-training independent practice (performing under a full and unrestricted license) in the United States; OR (3) Non-US residency training programs followed by a minimum of three years of verified independent practice in the United States (performing under a full and unrestricted license) performing duties related to the position they are applying for (United States fellowships would be creditable towards this requirement), which the local Medical Staff Executive Committee deems to have provided the applicant with appropriate professional training and believes has exposed the Physician to an appropriate range of patient care experiences.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

In rare and unusual circumstances, the Facility Director can submit a memo to the VISN Director through the VISN Chief Medical Officer, who may approve requests for reasonable exceptions to the residency training requirement for Physicians whose composite record of experience, accomplishments, performance, and qualifications warrant such action.

The physician is responsible for the overall medical care and clinical practice for the HBPC Program. The incumbent is responsible for the day-to-day operations including assignments, ensuring coverage and working collaboratively with several other service lines to accomplish the mission.

The incumbent ensures the quality and timeliness of care provided, customer satisfaction, as well as compliance with standards of accrediting bodies such as The Joint Commission (TJC) and the Office of Inspector General (OIG). Medical care includes identifying the patient's medical problems, diagnosing and treating appropriately, determining the need for consultation from subspecialty care for specialized medical, surgical or psychiatric services and determining the need for services that may require transferring patients to other VA on Non-VA healthcare facilities, community nursing homes or discharge when appropriate.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

The VA North Texas Health Care System is seeking a highly qualified Psychiatrist to join the Residential Rehabilitation Treatment Program (RRTP), a dynamic multidisciplinary program providing comprehensive mental health and addiction treatment services to Veterans.

This residential program specializes in recovery-focused care for Veterans experiencing addictions and substance use disorders. The incumbent must possess strong skills in general outpatient psychiatry and addiction psychiatry, with demonstrated experience in diagnostic evaluations, pharmacotherapy, and psychotherapy.

The role requires competency in treating a wide range of clinical conditions such as substance use disorders; mood, anxiety, and psychotic disorders; post-traumatic stress disorder; and psychiatric conditions prevalent among elderly Veterans.

This position functions as part of a multidisciplinary mental health team at the Dallas VA Medical Center and collaborates closely with all residential programs across VANTHCS. The incumbent is encouraged to engage in the education and training of medical students, psychiatry residents, and addiction psychiatry fellows.

Responsibilities also include providing clinical supervision to Nurse Practitioners, Physician Assistants, and other allied health professionals, and serving as a collaborating physician when appropriate.

The Mental Health Service at VANTHCS delivers a full continuum of psychiatric and psychosocial services, including general adult and geriatric psychiatry, psychosomatic medicine, trauma-focused programs, substance use specialty care, psychosocial rehabilitation and recovery services, homelessness programs, peer support services, opiate replacement therapy, intensive case management, vocational rehabilitation, domiciliary-based services, and inpatient mental health care.

The facility supports active research initiatives in addiction psychiatry, post-traumatic stress disorder, disaster psychiatry, mood disorders, and homelessness. It also hosts extensive clinical training programs for medical students, psychiatry residents and fellows, psychology trainees, social workers, and nursing professionals.

VA North Texas Health Care System maintains strong academic partnerships with multiple affiliated institutions. VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package. VHA Physician Total Rewards. Louis Health Care System The responsibilities include preoperative evaluation, intraoperative anesthesia, postoperative care, and acute pain management. The physician will work in accordance with the facility's policies, procedures, and guidelines.

Duties and Responsibilities: Preoperative Evaluation: Conduct thorough preoperative assessments including obtaining patients' medical histories, performing physical examinations, Order and interpret necessary preoperative tests and investigations.

Develop individualized anesthesia care plans suited to the patient's clinical needs and procedural requirements and reviewing diagnostic tests and lab results.

Determine risk factors and plan anesthesia care. lntraoperative Anesthesia: Administer anesthesia (general, regional, local) to patients undergoing surgical, diagnostic, or therapeutic procedures.

Anesthesia Administration Administer various types of anesthesia, including general, regional, local, and sedation, based on the nature of the procedure and patient-specific factors. Monitor patients during procedures, adjusting anesthetics as necessary.

Utilize a range of techniques such as inhalation agents, intravenous medication, nerve blocks, and spinal or epidural anesthesia. Implement and follow safety protocols to minimize the risk of adverse reactions and complications. Postoperative Care: Provide postoperative care to ensure patients safely recover from anesthesia.

Manage pain and address any complications that may arise. Oversee the recovery of patients from anesthesia in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU). Assess and manage postoperative pain using multimodal analgesia techniques. Address postoperative complications related to anesthesia, such as nausea, vomiting, delirium, or respiratory issues.

Pain Management: Assess and manage acute and chronic pain in patients. Devise and implement pain management plans. Critical Care: Provide anesthesiology services in critical care environments, including intensive care units (ICU).

Manage critically ill patients, addressing issues related to ventilation, hemodynamic instability, and multi-organ support. Cardiac Anesthesia: Provide anesthesia care alone and/or with nurse anesthetists, and/or with student nurse anesthetists and anesthesia residents.

Administrative duties include participation in hospital committees, academic presentations, and participation in M and M, and Performance Improvement activities.

Provide anesthesia care to all Cardiac Cases, Structural Heart Procedures and perform Intra-op TEE (TEE certification recommended) Education and Training: Participate in the education and training of medical students, residents, and other healthcare professionals. Provide mentorship and guidance as appropriate.

Quality Improvement: Engage in continuous quality improvement processes. Participate in departmental or facility committees to improve patient care and services. As the Emergency Department (ED) physician you will provide emergent and urgent medical care for patients of all ages who present to the ALMD ED. Care encompasses stabilization, evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of the full spectrum of conditions within Emergency Medicine, including acute occupational health injuries and illnesses.
